To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the information transfer model is a useful tool for in silico primer-template similarity analysis, and the algorithm based on this model is useful for in silico PCR product prediction and gene finding.
a new information-theoretical method for primer-template similarity prediction was developed and successfully applied in in silico PCR.
the new algorithm is based on the hypothesis of information transfer and the information coefficient is calculated to measure the fidelity of this process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new algorithms and software tools for sequence analysis.
the development of a new algorithm for assessing the similarity between a primer and a template sequence based on the information theory.
the development of a novel algorithm for the in silico prediction PCR product from a whole genome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the information coefficient is a good measure for similarity between primer and annealing sites on template, and can be used as a criterion for in silico PCR product prediction.
the algorithm is a promising tool for predicting PCR products with a whole genome as template.
this algorithm is useful for the prediction of PCR products and gene finding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the information coefficient is a measure of similarity and can be used for prediction of PCR products.
information theory provides a new way for assessing similarity between two sequences and this way can be applied in many areas in bioinformatics.
the information transfer process between primer and template is a measure for the similarity between the two.
The main takeaway from our work is that
information theory-based algorithm for assessing similarity is an alternative to traditional methods based on sequence alignment and can provide a more objective measure of similarity.
the new algorithm is based on the fundamental concept of information transfer and is not a mere statistical correlation of two vectors of nucleotides.
the information theory-based algorithm is a useful approach to assess similarity between primer and annealing site.
